title: ts-sdk-polyfills-and-patterns-for-streaming-interop
creator: Sofia Zhang
description: Provide a small set of officially supported TypeScript helper utilities and guidance to make async-iterator <-> Web ReadableStream interop reliable across runtimes (Node/Deno/Browser/Edge) and compatible with the SDK's streaming APIs. This ticket captures the proposal, example patterns, compatibility constraints, and a minimal polyfill surface so integrations and reference apps can adopt streaming ergonomics without ad-hoc fragile code.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal helper module is published in the monorepo (packages/ts-sdk/stream-utils) exposing toWebReadable, toAsyncIterator, and wrapWithCancellation
Helpers are typed for TypeScript and emit declaration files; build passes in Node 18+, Deno flags and bundlers (esbuild/rollup)
Backpressure semantics: await for writable backpressure where available, and provide a best-effort fallback that queues up to a configurable limit
Cancellation propagates from AbortSignal/AbortController to AsyncIterator.return() and to the underlying stream controller
Examples + docs updated in SDK README with 3 examples: Node fetch -> SDK, browser fetch -> SDK, and serverless (Edge) usage
Integration test(s) demonstrating retry-on-idempotent-chunk-fail + resume behavior using synthetic network faults
proposed_solution:
Ship a small, well-documented helper module with three core utilities and a recommended pattern guide:

1) toWebReadable(asyncIterable, {highWaterMark, onCancel}): converts an AsyncIterator to a ReadableStream (Web/WHATWG) exposing backpressure via controller.desiredSize when available. Uses pull loop that awaits iterator.next() and controller.enqueue(chunk). Honors controller.close() and handles iterator.return() on cancellation.

2) toAsyncIterator(readableStream, {signal}): converts a ReadableStream into an async iterator that yields chunks and forwards cancellation to stream.getReader().cancel(). This helps existing SDK consumers that prefer for-await-of.

3) wrapWithCancellation(streamOrIterator, abortSignal): a lightweight adapter that ensures AbortSignal triggers both underlying cancel/cancelReader and iterator.return, and surfaces a clear CancelError.

Key ergonomics: maintain single-API surface in SDK docs (we recommend consumers use for-await-of for Node/Server apps and ReadableStream for browser DOM consumers) and provide these helpers as explicit exports. Implementation will avoid Node stream2/stream.Readable conversions (no native.stream dependency) to keep bundle size small; instead, detect environment and use global.ReadableStream when present or a tiny ponyfill otherwise.

Edge cases: for environments without controller.desiredSize we implement a bounded queue with configurable highWaterMark and backpressure applied by awaiting a promise producer when queue is full. Retry semantics are handled at the SDK call-layer: streaming transport layer will expose a retry hook that can replay idempotent chunks when safe. The helpers only provide deterministic cancellation and backpressure signals, not automatic retry of partial streams.
alternatives_considered: Rely on consumers to write ad-hoc adapters (rejected: leads to many subtle bugs and duplicate work)
Wrap Node stream.Readable <-> WHATWG stream in the SDK (rejected: adds 4-6KB + complexity and causes differences in browser bundles)
Publish helpers as a separate small npm package (considered; deferred because we prefer single-source in monorepo initially)
Provide only documentation (rejected: docs alone proved insufficient in prior incidents where consumers built incompatible cancellation semantics)
updates: 2025-02-15: Ticket created. Initial scope drafted after sync with DX and runtime teams. Noted common failures from support tickets: stalled streams in Edge runtimes and uncaught AbortSignal mismatches.

2025-02-19: Spike completed by @Mateo Ruiz. Prototype converters implemented and tested against node18, chrome, and deno. Prototype found two issues: (1) lack of desiredSize in Safari, (2) AbortSignal not forwarded properly when converting to async iterator. Documented workarounds.

2025-02-23: Design sync with SDK maintainers and Serving runtime. Decided on bounded queue fallback for missing desiredSize and explicit wrapWithCancellation API name. Agreed to avoid exposing retry logic in this module to keep responsibilities clear.

2025-02-27: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842 (prototype -> stream-utils). Added unit tests for cancellation and queue backpressure. Requesting review from @Ava Patel (DX) and @Ravi Desai (runtime).

2025-03-02: Addressed review comments: improved typings, added example patterns for resumable generators, added guidance for idempotent chunk boundaries in docs. Marking in-progress to finish integration tests and CI flakiness checks.
implementation_notes: Keep runtime detection minimal: prefer globalThis.ReadableStream if available. Ponyfill path should be a small ES module that only implements ReadableStream semantics needed by SDK (enqueue, close, desiredSize shim). Ensure tree-shaking friendly exports. Add CI matrix rows for Node18, Node20, Deno, latest Chrome Headless, and WebKit.
